sections.h2: Selling a house in Tredyffrin Township
sections.html:
Tredyffrin is the most populous township in Chester County, with 31,927 residents at the 2020 census, spread over 19.9 square miles of the Philadelphia Main Line. Its communities include Chesterbrook, Strafford, Howellville and East Howellville, plus portions of Paoli and Wayne.

Housing here ranges from colonial-era log houses and an 1818 octagonal schoolhouse to the postwar subdivisions that filled in after the population jumped from 7,836 to 16,004 between 1950 and 1960. Age and condition vary widely from street to street, so price off nearby sales instead of a township average.

Water can matter for a Tredyffrin sale, depending on your street. The township's 2025 annual report lists stormwater projects at Crabby Creek, Strafford Park, Bair Road, the Willis, Woodcrest and Upper Weadley Roads area, and Gregory Lane.

The township also runs flood buyouts. It received more than $697,000 to acquire the home at 595 Park Ridge Drive, demolish it and return the lot to vegetation, and more acquisitions were underway on Park Ridge Drive and Yellow Springs Road. If your home sits near Trout Creek or one of those streets, expect buyers and their insurers to ask about flood history, and gather repair records before you list.

sections.h2: Is an inspection or occupancy permit required to sell?
sections.html:
No. Tredyffrin has no resale inspection, and its Use and Occupancy permit is "not required for changes in residential ownership or tenancy." The permit applies to new residential construction. Commercial properties are different: a change of occupant, change of use or commercial alteration needs a U&O permit before occupancy.

Open permits are the practical risk. Applications go through the Clariti online portal, and final inspections must pass before a U&O is issued, so a deck or finished basement built without sign-off can surface during a buyer's inspection review. Residential plans get a maximum review of 15 business days. Email permits@tredyffrin.gov or call 610-644-1400 and press 4.

Some repairs need no building permit: painting, window replacement without structural change, replacing siding, replacing gutters, and re-roofing up to 25 percent of the roof in a 12 month span. Larger work and any change to plumbing, gas, mechanical or electrical systems does need one.

  • Removing more than five trees six inches or wider in diameter within 12 months needs a tree removal permit, unless the trees are dead or hazardous.
  • A student home is limited to three tenants and needs a special exception and registration.
  • Zoning certificates are requested by letter to the zoning officer, with the address and tax parcel.

sections.h2: Transfer tax and recording in Chester County
sections.html:
The Chester County Recorder of Deeds collects transfer tax for all 73 municipalities and the state. The usual rate is 1 percent to the state and 1 percent to the municipality, with Coatesville, Malvern and Tredyffrin as exceptions. Tredyffrin is set at 1.5 percent, so the local share here is higher than in most of the county.

Transfer tax rates and payment rules at recording in Tredyffrin
Charge or ruleAmount or method
State realty transfer tax1% of consideration or computed value
Tredyffrin municipal transfer tax1.5%, an exception to the county's usual 1%
Combined rate2.5%
Payment at recordingBusiness check, cashier check or money order to the Recorder of Deeds

The Recorder does not take cash or credit cards for transfer tax. Tax is figured on the price or on the computed value, which the county says is usually the higher figure. Pennsylvania makes both buyer and seller liable to the state, so settle in the contract who pays. Recorded documents usually show up in the county's online records within 48 hours, and a lender has 60 days to record a satisfaction after a payoff.

Chester County sets assessments, and appeals go to the county Board of Assessment Appeals. An annual appeal can be filed from May 1 through August 1, or the next business day if August 1 is a weekend. The decision takes effect with the next year's tax bills. If a change notice follows a new addition or permit, an interim appeal must be filed within 40 days of the notice.

Filing costs $25 for a residential parcel, paid by check or money order to the Chester County Treasurer. Forms must be printed and delivered, with no fax or electronic copies, to the Assessment Office at 313 W. Market Street, Suite 4202, West Chester. Hearings take place in the Government Services Center on Westtown Road, and you can bring recent sales of similar homes, an appraisal and exterior photographs from the last six months. A further appeal to the Court of Common Pleas must be filed within 30 days of the Board's notice.

The county's assessment represents 100 percent of market value at the base year, so it reflects that older value, which can sit well away from what a buyer would offer.

Schools come from the Tredyffrin-Easttown School District. The township approved turning an office building at 1200 Swedesford Road in Berwyn into a new elementary school, expected to open for the 2027-28 school year. A new school near a street can change how buyers talk about that neighborhood, so check the district's attendance map before you price.

  • Note whether your street is near a turnpike, 202 or 422 interchange, since noise comes up in showings.
  • Ask the district which school your address feeds, and say so in the listing.
  • Mention commuter rail access in Paoli if you are within a short drive.

sections.h2: What to bring to the township and the closing
sections.html:
Before you accept an offer, gather the papers each office will ask for. From the Permits and Inspections office, get a list of permits on your address and confirm none are open. From your lender, get a payoff letter. From your files, pull the deed and any receipts for roof, drainage or electrical work.

At closing the title agent adds up the payoff, any tax balance and the transfer tax, then records the deed with the county. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal, so the schedule depends mostly on the title search and on how fast open permits get closed out.

sections.h2: What are your options to sell quickly?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who purchases as-is. Buyers in this township are used to renovating, so a house that needs updating still draws interest.

  • List when the house is in good shape and you can handle showings.
  • Sell for cash when there are open permits, tenants, an estate to settle or repairs you cannot fund.
  • Pull the permit history from the township before any offer, because unresolved work can slow either route.

Compare offers on net proceeds after the 2.5 percent combined transfer tax, any agent fees and repairs, and ask each buyer in writing about closing dates.

faqs.q: Does Tredyffrin Township require a use and occupancy permit when I sell my house?
faqs.a: Not for an ordinary residential sale. The permit is not required for changes in residential ownership or tenancy, and it applies to new residential construction and to commercial occupancy changes.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax rate in Tredyffrin?
faqs.a: The county lists 1 percent to the state and 1.5 percent to Tredyffrin, a combined 2.5 percent. Most Chester County municipalities charge 1 percent on the local side.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Chester County assessment?
faqs.a: An annual appeal window runs from May 1 through August 1 each year. An interim appeal must be filed within 40 days of the date on an assessment change notice.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Tredyffrin house with open permits?
faqs.a: You can try, but open permits are a title and inspection problem. Ask Permits and Inspections at 610-644-1400 (press 4) which permits remain open, and finish the inspections first if you can.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed after closing in Tredyffrin?
faqs.a: With the Chester County Recorder of Deeds. The office takes transfer tax by business check, cashier check or money order, and posts records online within about 48 hours.
